descriptionChirho: The common noun for lion (אַרְיֵה) in its plural/determined forms, referring to the large predatory feline known throughout the ancient Near East. Multilingual evidence is consistent: eng 'lions/like-lion', spa 'leones/león', hin 'सिंहों/सिंह', arb 'الأُسُودِ/أَسَدٍ', kor '사자들/사자', swa 'simba/kama-simba'. The two clusters differ only in number (plural definite 'the lions' vs. singular with comparative preposition כ 'like a lion'), both referring to the literal animal. The simile construction is syntactic, not a metaphorical sense shift of the noun itself.
